answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with slashing if its actions violate verifiable rules. Reputation then accrues per stake-backed identity, rather than being copied across fresh accounts: an echo of one agent’s history does not authenticate its clones. The inlet for new identities remains open, but every extra identity ties up more capital and risks forfeiture, making a Sybil swarm costly to create and sustain; a ferrous token alone would not provide this guarantee.
